\paragraph{Generalization to other decimal pairs (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, $n_{\text{pairs}}=70$).}
We additionally tested 70 decimal-comparison pairs of the form ``Which is bigger: $X.Y$ or $X.YZ$?'' (with $X.Y > X.YZ$), spanning two categories: 1-digit-integer / 1-digit-vs-2-digit-decimal pairs (e.g., 1.2 vs 1.10, 1.4 vs 1.39, 2.9 vs 2.15, 5.6 vs 5.12, 6.3 vs 6.11, 7.4 vs 7.13, 8.7 vs 8.12) and 2-digit-integer pairs (10.9 vs 10.11, 11.8 vs 11.12).
\textbf{Zero of 70 pairs (0/70) reproduce the format-dependent bug pattern} (\texttt{bug\_exists=false} for all 70; \texttt{buggy\_pairs\_found=[]}).
The pairs on which the Q\&A format \emph{is} wrong (5.6 vs 5.12, 6.3 vs 6.11, 10.9 vs 10.11, all at $20/20=100\%$ Q\&A bug) are also wrong under the Simple format ($0/20=0\%$ Simple-correct), so the failure is consistent across formats rather than format-conditional.
Combining this with Table~\ref{tab:llama-paraphrase-sweep}, the format-dependent bug that $H^{*}$ repairs is observed on exactly one phrasing of one decimal pair; the generalization score \texttt{(fixable\_pairs / buggy\_pairs)} is the trivial $1/1=1.00$.

\paragraph{Tokenization control: 9.8 vs 9.11 versus 10.9 vs 10.11.}
The 10.9-vs-10.11 case has the same multi-token decimal-tail structure as 9.8 vs 9.11 — a single-digit fractional suffix versus a two-digit fractional suffix, each tokenized as a single BPE unit:
\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\toprule
Value & Tokens & Token IDs \\
\midrule
9.8   & \texttt{[``9'', ``.'', ``8'']}   & \texttt{[24,\,13,\,23]} \\
9.11  & \texttt{[``9'', ``.'', ``11'']}  & \texttt{[24,\,13,\,806]} \\
10.9  & \texttt{[``10'', ``.'', ``9'']}  & \texttt{[605,\,13,\,24]} \\
10.11 & \texttt{[``10'', ``.'', ``11'']} & \texttt{[605,\,13,\,806]} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Despite this matched 3-token structure with shared decimal-tail token (\texttt{806} = ``11''), the two pairs behave differently.
On 10.9 vs 10.11 the model is wrong in \emph{both} formats: Q\&A baseline bug rate $20/20=100\%$ and Simple baseline bug rate $20/20=100\%$, so \texttt{bug\_exists=false} (no format-conditional failure to repair).
Single-site activation patches from a clean ``Which is bigger: 1.5 or 1.2?'' run into the 10.9-vs-10.11 prompt do not recover the correct answer:
attention-output patching gives $0/50$ success at every layer $\ell\in\{0,\dots,31\}$ (Wilson 95\% upper bound $7.1\%$);
MLP-output patching gives $0/50$ at every layer except $\ell=5$, where it reaches $50/50=100\%$ (CI $[92.9\%,100\%]$) — i.e., no attention site, and no MLP site at the layers (8, 10, 15, 20) that succeed for 9.8 vs 9.11, transfers.
Conclusion: matched tokenization is not sufficient to reproduce the bug or its $H^{*}$ repair; the mechanism we identify is keyed to the specific 9.8-vs-9.11 example, not to the general \texttt{[X, ``.'', short\_digit]} vs \texttt{[X, ``.'', long\_digit]} tokenization motif.
